subtitle: Boasts on Copper, Footprints on the Ganges

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a royal figure on a riverbank, distant Ganges gleaming under a hazy sky
panels.action: Ratnapala stands in ornate Kamarupa armour at a misty river edge, one hand resting on his sword, the other holding a rolled copperplate, as a vast river plain fades into the horizon.

dialogue.text: In Ratnapala’s copperplates, Kamarupa’s king terrifies half of India—yet in the dust of Bengal, only one hard trail of footprints reaches the Ganges.

i18n.hi: रत्नपाल की ताम्रपत्रों में, कामरूप का राजा आधे भारत को डराता है—पर बंगाल की धूल में, गंगा तक बस एक सख्त पगचिह्नों की रेखा पहुँचती है।

panels.shot: slow aerial glide over the Brahmaputra valley, early morning mist hanging over forests and rivers
panels.action: Dense green hills and braided channels of the Brahmaputra stretch below, with scattered wooden villages and a distant fortified town rising on a low ridge.

dialogue.text: In the 10th century, the old kingdom of Kamarupa watched the world from the eastern hills, its kings guarding the Brahmaputra where India’s plains met the forests of Assam.

i18n.hi: दसवीं सदी में, पुराना कामरूप राज पूर्वी पहाड़ियों से दुनिया निहारता था, उसके राजा वहीं ब्रह्मपुत्र की रखवाली करते थे जहाँ भारत की मैदानी ज़मीन असम के जंगलों से मिलती थी।

panels.shot: interior wide of a royal hall, with a focus on youthful Ratnapala in the background amid courtiers
panels.action: Young Ratnapala, robed but unarmed, stands behind a seated elder king in a wooden-pillared hall, watching scribes and ministers argue over palm-leaf documents and maps on a low table.

dialogue.text: Ratnapala rose from this valley, heir to the Pala dynasty of Kamarupa, as older powers in the north—Bengal’s Palas and eastern Samatata—jostled over rivers and trade routes.

i18n.hi: यहीं की घाटी से उठा रत्नपाल, कामरूप की पाल वंश की कड़ी, जब उत्तर में पुराने ताकतवर—बंगाल के पाल और पूर्वी समतट—नदियों और व्यापार पर भिड़ रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Ratnapala examining a copperplate in lamplight
panels.action: An older Ratnapala, now in simple royal ornaments, leans over a freshly inscribed copperplate held by a court scribe, the metal glinting in lamplight as he traces the engraved letters with one finger.

dialogue.text: His court would later etch his name onto copper, as kings did, praising his virtues, his faith, and his victories. In those lines, his shadow swelled far beyond the hills.

i18n.hi: बाद में उसका दरबार, राजाओं की रीति से, उसका नाम तांबे पर उकेरता है—उसकी प्रशंसा, उसकी आस्था, उसकी जीतें। उन पंक्तियों में उसकी छाया पहाड़ियों के परे तक फैल जाती है।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of Ratnapala before a copperplate being engraved
panels.action: Ratnapala stands tall beside an engraver seated on the floor, who hammers delicate letters into a gleaming copperplate, while courtiers listen as a poet chants the draft aloud.

dialogue.text: The Gachtal plates sing that Ratnapala frightened Saka, Gurjara, Gauda, Kerala, Arab and southern kings—boasts of a Kamarupa lion whose roar shook every region around him.

i18n.hi: गछताल ताम्रपत्र गाते हैं कि रत्नपाल ने शक, गुर्जर, गौड़, केरल, अरब और दक्षिण के राजाओं को दहला दिया—कामरूप के उस शेर की शेखी, जिसकी दहाड़ ने चारों दिशाएँ हिला दीं।

panels.shot: tight focus on the engraver’s chisel over copper, with faint ghostly images of distant courts in the background
panels.action: The chisel meets copper in a close-up, while in the blurred background appear faint imagined silhouettes of distant kings—turbaned Gurjaras, seafaring southerners, Arab traders—like mirages around the plate.

dialogue.text: Yet inscriptions praise like this are panegyrics—royal poetry meant to magnify. Historians look past the glow, asking: which of these roaring claims left marks outside Ratnapala’s own court?

i18n.hi: पर ऐसे अभिलेख राज–स्तुति हैं—दरबारी कविता, जो बढ़ा–चढ़ाकर गाती है। इतिहासकार चमक के पार देख पूछते हैं: इन दहाड़ों में से कौन–सी सचमुच रत्नपाल की सीमा के बाहर भी निशान छोड़ गई?

panels.shot: map-like bird’s-eye, stylised, of eastern India with Kamarupa, Gauda and Samatata highlighted
panels.action: A stylised parchment-map view shows Kamarupa in the northeast, Gauda in Bengal’s heart, and Samatata near the eastern delta, with dotted lines sketched along rivers linking them.

dialogue.text: For most far-flung enemies in his copperplates, the trail ends at his own borders. But for Gauda—Bengal’s heart—and the eastern land of Samatata, another voice speaks from another plate.

i18n.hi: उसके ताम्रपत्रों के ज़्यादातर दूर के दुश्मन उसकी ही सीमा पर आकर थम जाते हैं। पर गौड़—बंगाल का दिल—और पूर्व का समतट, इनके लिए एक और ताम्रपत्र से दूसरी आवाज़ उठती है।

panels.shot: wide of a Chandra court in Samatata, contrasting with Kamarupa’s wooden hall
panels.action: In a different palace with coastal motifs, Chandra king Srichandra sits on a carved throne as envoys from the west and north stand before him, palm-leaf letters in their hands.

dialogue.text: Far to the southeast, in Samatata, ruled Srichandra of the Chandra line. His own Dacca copperplate would later recall how Kamarupa’s campaigns pulled Bengal and Samatata into the same storm.

i18n.hi: दूर दक्षिण–पूर्व के समतट में, चंद्र वंश के श्रीचन्द्र राज करते थे। उनके ही ढाका ताम्रपत्र ने बाद में लिखा कि कामरूप के युद्धों ने कैसे बंगाल और समतट को एक ही आँधी में घसीट लिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Chandra scribe composing the Dacca copperplate
panels.action: A Chandra scribe, hair tied back, sits cross-legged engraving a copperplate while another courtier dictates, palm-leaf in hand, gesturing toward a painted map on the wall.

dialogue.text: The Dacca plate does not care for Ratnapala’s glory. It remembers instead how Srichandra stepped into Bengal’s troubles, helping restore Rajyapala’s line after Kamarupa armies intruded into the Brahmaputra-Gauda corridor.

i18n.hi: ढाका का पत्र रत्नपाल की महिमा नहीं गिनता। वह याद रखता है कि कैसे श्रीचन्द्र ने बंगाल की उलझन में पाँव रखा, जब कामरूप की सेनाएँ ब्रह्मपुत्र–गौड़ मार्ग में घुस आईं तो राज्यपाल की कड़ी को वापस सँभालने मदद की।

panels.shot: wide shot of Ratnapala addressing his generals in a riverside camp
panels.action: Ratnapala, armour gleaming, stands on a raised platform in a bamboo-fenced camp by a broad river, pointing west as armoured soldiers, elephants and standard-bearers listen with tightened faces.

dialogue.speaker: ratnapala
dialogue.text: Gauda’s weakness is our tide. We march while the river favours us.

i18n.hi: गौड़ की दुर्बलता ही हमारी लहर है। नदी साथ दे रही है, हम बढ़ते हैं।

panels.shot: long lateral shot of an army column moving along a riverbank toward the plains
panels.action: A long column of Kamarupa troops, elephants and horsemen winds along a muddy riverbank, Ratnapala riding near the front beneath a banner marked with a stylised lion, forests thinning into flatter plains.

dialogue.text: The Kamarupa records, and the later tradition built on them, speak of Ratnapala pressing westward—into Gauda’s orbit—taking advantage of the turbulence in Bengal’s royal house.

i18n.hi: कामरूप के लेख, और उन पर बनी परंपरा, बताते हैं कि रत्नपाल पश्चिम की ओर—गौड़ की कक्षा में—धकेलता है, बंगाल के राज–घराने की हलचल का मौका उठाकर।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Bengal palace in confusion as news arrives
panels.action: Inside a Gauda palace courtyard, courtiers cluster around a breathless messenger who gestures eastward, while guards look uneasily toward the distant gate.

dialogue.text: Rajyapala of Bengal, a Pala ruler whose grip on Gauda was already tested by rivals, now faced pressure from the east. Kamarupa’s move pushed into the contested lands between their realms.

i18n.hi: बंगाल के राज्यपाल, पाल राजा, जिनकी पकड़ पहले ही गौड़ पर टकराव झेल रही थी, अब पूरब से दबाव झेलते हैं। कामरूप का धक्का दोनों के बीच की विवादित जमीन पर चढ़ आता है।

panels.shot: somber interior shot of a royal harem corridor in Bengal, with guards escorting a veiled figure
panels.action: In a dim corridor lined with carved pillars, a veiled royal woman is hurried along by guards, while a small retinue follows, their faces tense; a doorway ahead opens to a courtyard where unfamiliar soldiers wait.

dialogue.text: The Dacca plate, looking back from Srichandra’s court, speaks of Kamarupa’s men seizing Rajyapala’s queen—a courtly note of humiliation and leverage, recorded coolly, without flourish.

i18n.hi: ढाका का पत्र, श्रीचन्द्र के दरबार से पीछे देखते हुए, लिखता है कि कामरूप के लोगों ने राज्यपाल की रानी को पकड़ लिया—दरबारी अपमान और दबाव की ठंडी, सीधी नोटिंग।

panels.shot: close-up of Srichandra listening to a Bengal envoy, faces half-lit
panels.action: Srichandra leans forward on his throne, expression thoughtful, as a Bengal envoy bows deeply, speaking earnestly, their faces lit by slanting light from a high window.

dialogue.text: For Srichandra’s scribes, the story turns here. They cast their king as the restorer—ally of Rajyapala’s line against Kamarupa’s incursion, intervening in the Brahmaputra-Gauda corridor to rebalance power.

i18n.hi: श्रीचन्द्र के लेखकों के लिए कहानी यहीं मोड़ लेती है। वे अपने राजा को बहाल करने वाला बताते हैं—राज्यपाल की कड़ी के साथी, कामरूप की घुसपैठ के खिलाफ, ब्रह्मपुत्र–गौड़ मार्ग में ताकत का संतुलन वापस करने वाले।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of Kamarupa and Chandra forces facing off across a flooded field
panels.action: Two distant lines of troops face each other across a waterlogged field under heavy clouds, banners of Kamarupa and Samatata visible above shield walls, with elephants restless at the edges.

dialogue.text: The details of the clash are lost; no chronicle names the field, no poet describes each manoeuvre. But the Chandra plate is clear that Kamarupa’s advance was checked and Gauda’s dynasty upheld with Samatata’s aid.

i18n.hi: टक्कर के बारीक दृश्य खो गए; कोई इतिहास किताब मैदान का नाम नहीं देती, कोई कवि चाल–दर–चाल नहीं गिनता। पर चंद्र ताम्रपत्र साफ कहता है कि कामरूप की बढ़त रोकी गई और समतट की मदद से गौड़ वंश टिकाया गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ratnapala on a riverboat returning upstream, pensive
panels.action: Ratnapala sits beneath a canopy on a large riverboat moving against the current, armour loosened, eyes fixed on the receding west bank as soldiers and oarsmen labour quietly around him.

dialogue.text: Whatever the intermediate turns, the outcome is plain in the shared record: Bengal’s line endured with Chandra support, and Kamarupa’s king withdrew upriver, his reach having brushed, not remade, Gauda.

i18n.hi: बीच–बीच के मोड़ जैसे भी रहे हों, साझा रिकॉर्ड का नतीजा साफ है: चंद्रों की सहारे से बंगाल की कड़ी बची रही, और कामरूप का राजा नदी के ऊपर लौट गया—उसकी पहुँच ने गौड़ को छुआ, बदला नहीं।

panels.shot: interior shot mirroring p03, Ratnapala again with a copperplate but older and more worn
panels.action: An older Ratnapala, hair streaked with grey, studies another copperplate in the same lamplit hall, his face marked by years, while a court poet waits, head bowed, holding a palm-leaf draft.

dialogue.text: Yet his plates still spoke of distant foes cowed by his name—the Saka, the Gurjara, the Arab, Kerala and the southern kings—claims that no other inscription, from any court, steps forward to confirm.

i18n.hi: फिर भी उसके पत्र दूर–दूर के दुश्मनों के झुकने की डींग हाँकते हैं—शक, गुर्जर, अरब, केरल और दक्षिण के राजा—दावे जिन्हें कोई और दरबार, कोई और शिलालेख आगे आकर नहीं दोहराता।

panels.shot: tight close-up on the engraved words on Ratnapala’s plate dissolving into blank parchment
panels.action: The etched letters on a copperplate fill the frame, then fade into an empty parchment surface, as if the words are being tested and some lines dissolve away.

dialogue.text: Here the historian steps in. D.C. Sircar and others separate the plates’ pan-Indian boasts from the firmer ground—seeing in Gauda and Samatata a real theatre of action, and elsewhere, the glow of royal exaggeration.

i18n.hi: यहीं इतिहासकार उतरते हैं। डी. सी. सरकार और दूसरे, इन ताम्रपत्रों की अखिल–भारतीय शेखियों को अलग रख, ठोस जमीन पर टिकते हैं—गौड़ और समतट में असली मोर्चा देखते हैं, और बाकी को राज–अतिशयोक्ति की चमक।

panels.shot: three-quarter shot of Ratnapala in profile looking toward a faint vision of the Ganges
panels.action: Ratnapala stands on a terrace above the Brahmaputra, in profile, the faint silhouette of another broad river—the imagined Ganges—overlaid beyond the horizon, as evening light softens his features.

dialogue.text: So Ratnapala’s step toward the Ganges survives not as empire, but as a contested campaign traced in copper from different courts—a reminder that true strength does not lie in louder boasts, but in what other voices also recall.

i18n.hi: इस तरह रत्नपाल का गंगा की ओर बढ़ा कदम साम्राज्य नहीं, बल्कि एक विवादित अभियान बनकर बचा है—अलग–अलग दरबारों की ताम्रपटों पर खिंची रेखाओं में—याद दिलाता हुआ कि असली ताकत ऊँची शेखियों में नहीं, उन यादों में है जिन्हें दूसरे भी दोहराएँ।

subtitle_i18n.en: Boasts on Copper, Footprints on the Ganges
subtitle_i18n.hi: ताम्र पर शेखी, गंगा पर पगचिह्न
